prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mathematics, physics, and chemistry acquired in the first year of the Degree program is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Students should be able to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation professionally and possess the competences typically demonstrated through the preparation and defense of arguments and problem-solving within their field of study.

Students should have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Students should be able to transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Ability to manage information, handle, and apply technical specifications and legislation necessary for engineering practice.
Ability to apply new technologies including information and communication technologies.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of materials science, technology, and chemistry. Understand the relationship between microstructure, synthesis or processing, and material properties.
Basic knowledge and application of environmental technologies and sustainability.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK 1. CRYSTALLINE STATE

THE SCIENCE OF MATERIALS. MATERIAL SELECTION. Materials Science: concept, relationship with Engineering and Industry. Engineering Materials: classification by bond type. Structure and properties of materials. Material selection in Engineering. APB: Material and process selection for specific designs.

CRYSTALLINE STRUCTURE. METALLIC CRYSTALS. States of matter. Crystalline and amorphous substances. Space lattices and unit cells. Crystalline systems, Bravais lattices. Isomorphism, polymorphism, and allotropy. Study of metallic lattices. Coordination number, atomic radius, packing factor. Voids in close-packed structures. Miller indices. Miller-Bravais indices in the HCP system. Interplanar distance. Volumetric, linear, and superficial densities.

CRYSTALLINE IMPERFECTIONS. The real solid. Influence of defects. Common crystalline structure defects. Point defects: vacancies, interstitials, impurities, Frenkel and Schottky defects. Line defects. Surface defects: twins, stacking faults, and grain boundaries.
BLOCK 2. ALLOYS

ALLOYS. Pure metals and alloys. Constitution of alloys: components and constituents. Solid solutions and mechanical mixtures. Types of Solid Solutions. Hume-Rothery rules. Properties of solid solutions. Determination of solid solution type. Intermediate phases: types and characteristics. Ordered solid solutions: superlattices.

HARDENING MECHANISMS AND RECRYSTALLIZATION PHENOMENA. Introduction. Grain refinement hardening. Alloying hardening. Precipitation hardening. Dispersion hardening. Quenching hardening. Strain hardening. Cold deformation: work hardening state. Variation of mechanical properties. Effects of heating: recovery, recrystallization, and grain growth. Recrystallization temperature. Hot working.
BLOCK 3: SOLIDIFICATION AND DIFFUSION

SOLIDIFICATION PROCESSES. Introduction. Solidification: homogeneous nucleation and heterogeneous nucleation. Magnitudes determining the process: nucleation and growth rates. Microstructure. Ingot solidification: structures. Structure control: grain size, shape, and orientation. Microstructural defects in solidification: segregations. Macrostructural defects: shrinkage cavities, blowholes, pores, cavities, cracks, and splashes. Rapid solidification: metallic glasses.
DIFFUSION. Introduction. Diffusion mechanisms. Volume diffusion: Fick's Laws. Factors influencing diffusion. Diffusion applications.
BLOCK 4: EQUILIBRIUM DIAGRAMS.

SYSTEM EQUILIBRIUM. EQUILIBRIUM DIAGRAMS I. Material system: components and phases. Systems in equilibrium: equilibrium factors and degrees of freedom. Phase rule (Gibbs' Law). Cooling curves. Two-component systems: experimental determination of diagrams. Mass distribution: lever rule. Interpretation rules.

EQUILIBRIUM DIAGRAMS II. Types of binary diagrams according to solid-state solubility. Diagrams of total solid-state solubility. Diagrams of total solid-state insolubility. Diagrams of partial solid-state solubility: eutectic and peritectic reactions. Solid-state transformations: allotropy, order-disorder transformations, eutectoid and peritectoid reactions. Complex diagrams: intermediate phases. Ternary diagrams. Non-equilibrium phase transformations.
BLOCK 5: METALLIC MATERIALS AND THEIR TREATMENTS

FERROUS ALLOYS: STEELS AND CAST IRONS. Introduction. Iron: allotropic states. Iron-cementite and iron-carbon diagrams. Classification of Fe-C alloys. Equilibrium phases and constituents: definition of structures. Invariant transformations. Critical points. Irons: types and characteristics. Steels: classifications and mechanical characteristics by type. Alloy steels: Influence of alloying elements. Influence on the Fe-Fe3C diagram. Alphagenic, gammagenic, and carbide-forming elements. Effect on TTT curves. Low and high alloy steels. Cast irons. Graphitizing and carbide-forming elements. White and malleable cast irons. Gray and spheroidal or ductile cast irons. Mechanical characteristics of cast irons.

ISOTHERMAL TRANSFORMATION DIAGRAM OF AUSTENITE. Introduction. Isothermal transformations of austenite. Pearlite and bainite. Martensitic transformation: properties. Relationship between cooling curves and T.I. diagrams. Continuous cooling curves and transformations.

HEAT TREATMENTS. Introduction. Classification and objectives of steel heat treatments. Annealing. Normalizing. Quenching. Quenching factors. Critical quenching rate. Hardenability. Jominy test. Tempering. Tempering transformations. Tempering diagrams. Surface treatments: thermal and thermochemical.

NON-FERROUS METALS AND ALLOYS. Introduction. Unalloyed aluminum. Properties and applications. Main aluminum alloys. Classification. Wrought alloys: heat treatments. Casting alloys: modification of Al-Si alloys. Properties and applications of aluminum alloys. Other light alloys. Unalloyed copper. Properties and applications. Work hardening in copper. Copper alloys: Brasses and Bronzes. Applications and treatments.
BLOCK 6: CORROSION AND ITS CONTROL
CORROSION AND PROTECTION. Introduction. Electrochemical fundamentals. Corrosion rate. Forms of corrosion. Corrosion protection. Coatings. Polymer degradation.
BLOCK 7: POLYMERIC MATERIALS

STRUCTURE, BEHAVIOR, AND PROCESSING OF POLYMERS. Introduction. Polymerization mechanisms. Polymer structure. General classification of polymers. Thermoplastics. Thermosets. Elastomers. Mechanical behavior of polymers.
BLOCK 8. CERAMIC MATERIALS. PROCESSING OF CERAMICS AND GLASSES

CERAMIC MATERIALS AND GLASSES. Introduction. Structure of ceramic materials. Ionic crystals. Silicate structures. Properties of ceramic materials. Non-crystalline ceramic materials: glasses. Glass transition temperature. Processing of ceramics and glasses.
BLOCK 9. COMPOSITE MATERIALS

COMPOSITE MATERIALS. MATRICES AND REINFORCEMENTS. Introduction. Concept of composite material. Matrix and reinforcement. Types of Matrices. Fiber reinforcement. Most commonly used materials. Particle reinforcement. Matrix considerations. Mechanical behavior. Applications.
BLOCK 10: MATERIAL TESTING

TENSILE TESTS. (In laboratory) Mechanical behavior of materials: intrinsic and extrinsic conditions. Normal and shear stresses. Elastic behavior: modulus of elasticity and yield strength. Plastic deformation: slip and twinning. Schmid's law. Tensile testing. Definitions. Test specimens. Diagrams. Ductile and brittle fracture. Test execution. Results.

HARDNESS TESTS. (In laboratory) Hardness: types. Classification of hardness measurement methods. Static indentation hardness tests: Brinell, Vickers, and Rockwell. Advantages and disadvantages. Other tests.

IMPACT AND TECHNOLOGICAL TESTS. (In laboratory) Ductility, malleability, brittleness, and toughness. Ductile and brittle fracture. Influencing factors. Resilience tests. Types and dimensions of test specimens. Charpy test. Izod test. Flexion test: fundamentals, flexion diagram. Technological tests: bending, deep drawing, forging, cutting, punching.

METALLOGRAPHIC TECHNIQUES. MACROSCOPY AND MICROSCOPY. (In laboratory). The metallographic laboratory. Macroscopy: preparation and etching. Macroscopic techniques. Microscopy: sample preparation phases. The metallographic microscope. Observation of different structural constituents. Grain size measurements.

NON-DESTRUCTIVE TESTS. (In laboratory) Visual inspection. Radiographic inspection. Equipment and operating techniques. Protection and safety measures. Ultrasonic inspection. Physical fundamentals. Nature and properties of ultrasonic waves. Equipment and operating techniques. Magnetic methods tests. Physical fundamentals. Techniques and equipment. Detection of surface cracks. Penetrant liquids.
BLOCK 11. BASIC CONCEPTS OF ENVIRONMENTAL TECHNOLOGIES
ENVIRONMENTAL TECHNOLOGY. Materials and environment. Environmental aspects of design. Urban and industrial waste. Recovery, reuse, and recycling.
Practical Work:
Tensile Test
Hardness tests
Impact test
Technological tests
Non-destructive tests
Metallography. Observation of different structural constituents and determination of grain size
teaching_methods: Exposition of theory and general examples

assessment_methods.method: Assistance and/or participation in face-to-face and/or virtual activities
Completion of assignments, cases or exercises (including practice report submission and problem solving)

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, a written exam (short questions and problem solving) is required, needing a minimum of 4 out of 10 points to be computable. Attendance and submission of laboratory practice reports are mandatory, and practices must be approved to pass the course. Active attendance and participation are evaluated through proposed problems and self-assessment questionnaires. In an extraordinary call, students can opt for a global assessment (a single theoretical/practical test) which allows them to pass the subject and obtain 100% of the grade.
